TextBlock.Text: THEATRE North of Biak
DATE 11 November 2028 · 0640 local
SIDE People's Liberation Army Navy
WINDOW 90 min, closes at 135
Y-9 special mission family. Photo: Alert5 · CC BY-SA 4.0 · cropped
"Simply stated, strategic deterrence is about communicating capability and intent."
- Adm. Cecil D. Haney, Commander, US Strategic Command

NORTH OF BIAK, 0640. At 2340 last night a torpedo hit the Russian detachment's auxiliary in the northern approaches. She is afloat and making six knots, and she is the Russian detachment's business, not this headquarters'. The boat that fired is not.

Nobody has claimed her. Fleet headquarters has designated her GOLF and wants a class on her before HAI YANG 7 goes into the northern roads tomorrow night. SEA EAR 31, the enclave detachment's Y-9, is airborne with a full load of buoys. GOLF has had seven hours, and she is assessed to be within thirty miles of where the auxiliary was hit, north-east of the aircraft.
A RAAF Poseidon is over the same water, recording. Leave it alone.

Put a class on GOLF, then bring the aircraft back over the enclave field. Fire nothing: SEA EAR 31 starts at weapons Hold, and a torpedo from it would be the group firing first on a boat it cannot name. Biak's fishing boats and a coaster bound for Jayapura are on the water.
COMMAND NET: A mission-specific tactical report follows eight minutes after the start. It is advice from the command team, not a new sensor detection.
Fleet headquarters
COMMANDER'S INTENT

The boat that fired last night is not ours and not the Russians', and the enclave's fuel goes in through her water tomorrow night. Know what she is. A class is a buoy pattern and patience; it is not a torpedo, and nothing the group launches today has a warhead on it. The Australian aircraft over the same water is recording. Give it nothing to record but an aircraft laying buoys.
• Classify the submarine, then bring Sea Ear 31 back over the enclave field
• Fire on nothing: not the boat, not the patrol aircraft
• Bring Sea Ear 31 home
• Classify the patrol aircraft over the buoy field
• Harm no fishing boat or coaster
Sea Ear 31, a Y-9 out of the enclave field, with sonobuoys. Opposing: one submarine, GOLF, unclaimed. Watching: a RAAF P-8A. Neutral: two Biak fishing boats and a coaster.

The planned window is 90 minutes. At that minute Command signals that you are behind schedule and holds the line for about 45 minutes more; the operation is closed at 135 minutes and the main task will be recorded as failed.
RULES OF ENGAGEMENT
All designated neutral contacts are protected. A protected neutral loss cancels the operation. Identify before you shoot.
